title: Man dies in police custody: Coroner investigating third death in less than two years under RCMP care
article: The coroner's office is investigating the death of a Prince George man one day after he was wrestled down and tasered by RCMP for allegedly resisting arrest.

RCMP say Clayton Alvin Wiley, 33, died Tuesday morning in hospital. An autopsy is being done in Kamloops, police said, but the cause of death was not known Tuesday. A coroner's investigation and inquest are mandatory whenever someone dies in police custody. The RCMP North District major crime section also investigates all in- custody deaths.
Ambulance attendants had to resuscitate Wiley on the way to hospital Monday evening, and he died at Prince George Regional Hospital about 16 hours later, RCMP spokesperson Const. Gary Godwin said.

The incident began around 5:15 p.m. Monday, after police received several complaints from residents of a man acting "irrationally and aggressively" in their backyards, in the 1600 block of 11th Avenue, Godwin said. Before police arrived, a security guard from the nearby Parkwood Place mall said he had found the man lying on the ground in the alley, and that Wiley had tried to punch him.
When three police officers arrived to arrest him for assault and causing a disturbance, Godwin said Wiley had to be physically restrained.

"He was wrestled to the ground and handcuffed. He didn't comply with verbal commands to lie down, put his hands behind his back and identify himself," Godwin said. He described Wiley as "immensely powerful," adding he was known to two of the officers at the scene.

Godwin said police had asked an ambulance to meet them at the RCMP detachment so the man's "irrational" behaviour could be assessed, but he struggled when police officers tried to place him in the ambulance. "When he got out of the police car, he was very aggressive and confrontational and wouldn't take verbal commands and had to be tasered," he said. Godwin couldn't say whether alcohol or drugs were involved.

Regional coroner Dave Coverdale confirmed his office is investigating the death, but wouldn't release any other information, deferring questions to RCMP. "It's inappropriate for me to answer these questions right now," he said Monday, saying he hadn't been fully informed about the case.
Wiley's is the third in-custody death in Prince George the coroner's office has investigated in less than two years.

An inquest into last September's death of Darrell Paquette, 43, who died while being arrested by an off-duty police officer at The Bay at Parkwood Place had been scheduled for June but was postponed. Last year, a jury at a coroner's inquest found Peter Benoit Prince, 64, died of natural causes after collapsing in police cells in November, 2001.

RCMP began using taser guns -- which shoot darts carrying electrical currents to create muscle spasms and cause a temporary collapse -- as part of a pilot project in 2000. A number of officers trained in the technique have since begun using the stun guns, along with other tools like pepper spray and batons, and Prince George RCMP have said they're effective in subduing a suspect with no lasting effects.
